method: Read every selected original pinned Hebrew verse and its written/read and other annotations before composing English.
Compose a connected reading voice, retaining source meaning, literary form, gender-specific relationships, ancient imagery, meaningful repetitions and consequential uncertainty.
Read every TSW comparator after drafting; compare at verse level and revise draft overinterpretations. No mechanical synonym substitution or overlap quota.
Record individual before/after text, rationale, F0–F3 editorial choice, exact original source-verse hash and comparator for every verse.
Reread selected source/English difficulties as an authoring check; independent editorial review and reader testing have not occurred.

source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of exact original XML verse substrings including written/read and other notes; no normalized reconstruction.
source.public_versification_note: 1 Kings 1: all 53 public verses bind one-to-one to matching Hebrew records.

comparison_limit: Normalized whole-verse overlap is triage, not evidence by itself of fidelity, originality or comprehension. Shared clear wording remains where appropriate.
companion_impact: All changed chapter quotations, hashes and reference bindings need reconciliation in a later authorized Companion installation; the separate Companion branch was not modified.
whole_book_consistency: Whole-book 1 Samuel and 2 Samuel authoring passes remain queued; this twenty-chapter draft and focused reread do not substitute for those passes.
independent_review_priority: 1:4: care distinguished from sexual relations; 1:6: birth sequence without an invented shared mother.
1:13,17,24–27: reports, questions and oaths attributed to their speakers; 1:27,47 read forms retained.
1:39,45: Zadok’s actual anointing and Jonathan’s report of Zadok and Nathan remain distinct.
1:50–53: altar horns and Solomon’s conditional response do not become an unconditional oath.
